1. The accused has been sent to face trial under Section 419/420/468/471 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter called as IPC), on the allegations that during the year 2002,
the accused approached SDM Rajouri Garden and other concerned authorities impersonating herself as daughter of Shri Ramey for issuance of SC Certificate and also submitted affidavit, claiming Digitally signed by VASUNDHARA VASUNDHARA CHHAUNKAR CHHAUNKAR FIR No.246/2002 State Vs. Secondly in the above said year she approached the SDM and other concerned authorities by filing an application and affidavit for issuance of SC Certificate and fraudulently claimed herself as daughter of Shri Ramey and on such inducement the concerned SDM had issued SC Certificate while in fact she was not her daughter thereby committed an offence punishable U/s 420 IPC. application for SC Certificate and the affidavit as genuine by submitting the same in the office of SDM/concerned authorities having reasons to believe that the same were forged documents thereby committed an offence punishable U/s 471 IPC. 
2. Cognizance for the said offence was taken and the accused was summoned. Copies were supplied to her and after arguments on charge, ld. Predecessor of this Court framed charges against accused Sunita Bharti on 01.11.2004 U/s 419/420/468/471 to which she pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. PW-1 Shri Vijay Khanna, Deputy Secretary Home, 5th Level, Delhi Secretariat,
New Delhi deposed that in the month of May 2000 he joined as SDM Rajouri Garden and he worked there till July 2002. During the course of his duties as SDM, Rajouri Garden, accused Sunita claiming herself to be daughter of Shri Ramey son of Shri Attar Singh, R/o C-48, Babu Park, Delhi moved an application dated 05.03.2002 for issuance of SC Certificate. Along-with an application she submitted an affidavit, copy of food card and cast certificate of Shri Ramey which she identified belonged to her father. Alongwith the above-said documents accused had also submitted schedule cast certificate (hereinafter referred to SC Certificate) of her husband Ghanshyam and moved an application form duly attested by Shri Shadi Ram, Member Legislative Assembly, Delhi. On receipt of application form alongwith documents the then Tehsildar marked the application alongwith documents for verification purpose to the concerned bailiff. The bailiff after verification submitted his report to Tehsildar and Tehsildar recommended the report of bailiff and the application alongwith documents were submitted to him. On the basis of the said documents as well as on the VASUNDHARA CHHAUNKAR CHHAUNKAR Date:

He further deposed that on the basis of application moved by accused SC Certificate in original was given to the accused and the counterfoil in respect of issuance of certificate in favour of accused Ex.PW1/D was issued by him and the same bear stamp of his office. 
He further deposed that after issuance of SC Certificate in favour of accused, a complaint was received in his sub-division District West regarding concealment of facts for issuance of said SC Certificate. On receipt of the complaint, an enquiry was conducted and during enquiry it was found that accused Sunita had concealed the facts in her affidavit and documents submitted by her and she had furnished wrong information in respect of her father. During the course of enquiry, Tehsildar called accused Sunita in his office to clarify qua submissions of wrong documents for SC Certificate. However, Sunita did not appear before him instead she sent her reply stating that the documents VASUNDHARA CHHAUNKAR CHHAUNKAR Date:

He further stated that the signatures on the documents submitted by accused Sunita vide her application dated 02.05.2002 does not bear his signatures. He further stated that the certificate which was attached with the application of Sunita is genuine but the same does not belong to him and submitted that accused Sunita is not her daughter. On the basis of the enquiry and after satisfying himself that accused Sunita had been able to procure cast certificate by furnishing false documents and information, a notice dated 28.06.2002 mark PX-4 was issued to her for surrendering the cast certificate in question for the purpose of cancellation. However, accused Sunita did not surrender the said certificate and thereafter he passed orders dated 10.7.2002 Ex.PW1/F cancelled the said SC Certificate issued in favour of accused Sunita. annotations.text: The sale deeds executed by first appellant, clearly and obviously do not fall under the second and third categories of false documents'.

It therefore remains to be seen whether the claim of the complainant that the execution of sale deeds by the first accused, who was in no way connected with the land, amounted to committing forgery of the documents with the intention of taking possession of complainant's land (and that accused 2 to 5 as the purchaser, witness, scribe and stamp vendor colluded with first accused in execution and registration of the said sale deeds) would bring the case under the first category.

There is a fundamental difference between a person executing a sale deed claiming that the property conveyed is his property, and a person executing a sale deed by impersonating the owner or falsely claiming to be authorised or empowered by the owner, to execute the deed on owner's behalf.
When a person executes a document conveying a property describing it as his, there are two possibilities.
The first is that he bonafide believes that the property actually belongs to him.
The second is that he may be dishonestly or fraudulently claiming it to be his even though he knows that it is not his property.
